quests.hint: This adjective describes a person who can express ideas clearly and effectively in speech.
quests.explanation: 'Articulate speaker,' 'highly articulate,' and 'articulate your thoughts' are key. 'Articulate' is both adjective and verb. 'Well-articulated argument' means clearly expressed.
quests.textToSpeak: She is an extremely ___ speaker who always explains complex ideas very clearly.
quests.correctAnswer: She is an extremely articulate speaker who always explains complex ideas very clearly.

quests.hint: This adjective describes writing or speech that is brief but contains all the essential information.
quests.explanation: 'Succinct explanation,' 'keep it succinct,' and 'a succinct summary' are key. More formal than 'brief' or 'short.' 'Succinctly' is the adverb: 'put it succinctly.'
quests.textToSpeak: Please keep your answer ___ - we have limited time for each candidate today.
quests.correctAnswer: Please keep your answer succinct - we have limited time for each candidate today.

quests.hint: This adjective describes something that is legal, genuine, or properly justified.
quests.explanation: 'Legitimate concern,' 'legitimate business,' and 'a legitimate reason' are key. 'Legitimately' is the adverb. 'Illegitimate' means not valid or not legally recognized.
quests.textToSpeak: She had a perfectly ___ reason for missing the meeting that everyone accepted.
quests.correctAnswer: She had a perfectly legitimate reason for missing the meeting that everyone accepted.

quests.hint: This adjective describes someone who focuses on practical solutions rather than theories.
quests.explanation: 'Pragmatic approach,' 'pragmatic decision,' and 'be pragmatic about' are key. 'Pragmatism' is the noun. 'Take a pragmatic view' means focus on what actually works in practice.
quests.textToSpeak: She took a very ___ approach to the problem rather than insisting on the ideal solution.
quests.correctAnswer: She took a very pragmatic approach to the problem rather than insisting on the ideal solution.

quests.hint: This adjective describes someone who can do many different things well and adapt easily.
quests.explanation: 'Versatile employee,' 'versatile performer,' and 'highly versatile' are key. 'Versatility' is the noun. A versatile skill set is very attractive to employers in changing markets.
quests.textToSpeak: She is an extremely ___ team member who can handle any task she is given.
quests.correctAnswer: She is an extremely versatile team member who can handle any task she is given.

quests.hint: This verb means to look at something very carefully to check it for errors or problems.
quests.explanation: 'Scrutinize accounts,' 'scrutinize a contract,' and 'under scrutiny' are key. 'Scrutiny' is the noun: 'public scrutiny.' 'Come under scrutiny' means to be examined carefully.
quests.textToSpeak: The committee will ___ every line of the report before it is officially published.
quests.correctAnswer: The committee will scrutinize every line of the report before it is officially published.

quests.hint: This adjective describes an organization or person that is open and honest about their actions.
quests.explanation: 'Transparent process,' 'be transparent about,' and 'transparency' are key. 'Transparency' (noun) is highly valued in governance and leadership. The opposite is 'opaque.'
quests.textToSpeak: Good leaders must be completely ___ about how decisions are made within their team.
quests.correctAnswer: Good leaders must be completely transparent about how decisions are made within their team.

quests.hint: This verb means to add something extra to make something more complete or effective.
quests.explanation: 'Supplement a diet,' 'supplement income,' and 'dietary supplement' are key. 'Supplement' is both noun and verb. 'In addition to' and 'alongside' are related connectors.
quests.textToSpeak: She decided to ___ her formal studies with an online course in graphic design.
quests.correctAnswer: She decided to supplement her formal studies with an online course in graphic design.

quests.hint: This adjective describes an action taken to prevent problems before they occur.
quests.explanation: 'Proactive approach,' 'proactive measures,' and 'be proactive about' are key. The opposite is 'reactive' - responding only after problems appear. 'Proactively' is the adverb.
quests.textToSpeak: Rather than waiting for issues to arise, she took a ___ approach to risk management.
quests.correctAnswer: Rather than waiting for issues to arise, she took a proactive approach to risk management.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a standard or reference point used for comparison and measurement.
quests.explanation: 'Set a benchmark,' 'industry benchmark,' and 'benchmark performance' are key. 'Benchmark' can be a noun or verb: 'benchmark against competitors.' Used in business and education.
quests.textToSpeak: They used the best-performing company in the sector as their ___ for success.
quests.correctAnswer: They used the best-performing company in the sector as their benchmark for success.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a rule, feature, or value used to judge or decide something.
quests.explanation: 'Meet the criterion,' 'the key criterion,' and 'assessment criteria' are key. 'Criteria' is the plural. 'Criterion-referenced' assessment measures against a fixed standard.
quests.textToSpeak: The most important ___ for selecting the winning project was real-world impact.
quests.correctAnswer: The most important criterion for selecting the winning project was real-world impact.

quests.hint: This verb means to publicly support or recommend a cause, idea, or person.
quests.explanation: 'Advocate for,' 'advocate change,' and 'strong advocate' are key. 'Advocate' can be a noun: 'a patient advocate.' 'Advocacy' is the noun for the activity.
quests.textToSpeak: She has spent her career ___ for greater equality in access to quality education.
quests.correctAnswer: She has spent her career advocating for greater equality in access to quality education.

quests.hint: This verb means to officially give out resources, time, or money for a specific purpose.
quests.explanation: 'Allocate resources,' 'allocate funding,' and 'allocate time' are key. 'Allocation' is the noun. 'Budget allocation' refers to where money is directed in an organization.
quests.textToSpeak: The government plans to ___ more funding to mental health services next year.
quests.correctAnswer: The government plans to allocate more funding to mental health services next year.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a general agreement among all or most members of a group.
quests.explanation: 'Reach a consensus,' 'build consensus,' and 'by consensus' are key. 'Consensus opinion' means the shared view. 'There is no consensus on' means people still disagree about it.
quests.textToSpeak: After hours of discussion, the team finally reached a ___ on the best way forward.
quests.correctAnswer: After hours of discussion, the team finally reached a consensus on the best way forward.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a difference between two things that should be the same.
quests.explanation: 'Identify a discrepancy,' 'unexplained discrepancy,' and 'discrepancy between' are key. 'Discrepancies in the accounts' suggests potential errors or fraud in financial records.
quests.textToSpeak: The auditor found a significant ___ between the reported and the actual figures.
quests.correctAnswer: The auditor found a significant discrepancy between the reported and the actual figures.

quests.hint: This adjective describes ideas or concepts that exist only in thought, not in physical form.
quests.explanation: 'Abstract concept,' 'abstract thinking,' and 'abstract art' are key. 'Abstraction' is the noun. 'Abstract' contrasts with 'concrete' - which refers to tangible, specific things.
quests.textToSpeak: Freedom is a highly ___ concept that different people understand very differently.
quests.correctAnswer: Freedom is a highly abstract concept that different people understand very differently.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a testable prediction or educated guess about why something happens.
quests.explanation: 'Form a hypothesis,' 'test a hypothesis,' and 'scientific hypothesis' are key. 'Hypothetical' is the adjective. 'A working hypothesis' is one being used as a temporary explanation.
quests.textToSpeak: The researchers tested their ___ by conducting a series of carefully controlled experiments.
quests.correctAnswer: The researchers tested their hypothesis by conducting a series of carefully controlled experiments.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a link or relationship between two variables that change together.
quests.explanation: 'Strong correlation,' 'positive correlation,' and 'correlation between X and Y' are key. Crucially, 'correlation does not imply causation' - they change together but one may not cause the other.
quests.textToSpeak: There is a well-established ___ between regular exercise and improved mental health.
quests.correctAnswer: There is a well-established correlation between regular exercise and improved mental health.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the conclusion you reach from evidence without being directly told.
quests.explanation: 'Draw an inference,' 'make an inference,' and 'reasonable inference' are key. 'Inferential reasoning' means drawing logical conclusions. 'Infer' is the verb: 'What can we infer?'
quests.textToSpeak: From her response, we can draw a clear ___ that she was not happy with the decision.
quests.correctAnswer: From her response, we can draw a clear inference that she was not happy with the decision.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the relationship where one thing directly causes another to happen.
quests.explanation: 'Establish causation,' 'prove causation,' and 'causation versus correlation' are key. Proving causation requires controlled experimentation. 'Causal link' means a proven cause-effect relationship.
quests.textToSpeak: The study was designed to prove ___, not just show that two factors are related.
quests.correctAnswer: The study was designed to prove causation, not just show that two factors are related.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the ability to understand and share the feelings of another person.
quests.explanation: 'Show empathy,' 'lack of empathy,' and 'empathy towards' are key. 'Empathise' is the verb. 'Empathetic' is the adjective. Empathy is often contrasted with 'sympathy' (feeling for someone).
quests.textToSpeak: Good leaders show genuine ___ toward their team members during difficult times.
quests.correctAnswer: Good leaders show genuine empathy toward their team members during difficult times.

quests.hint: This adjective describes an approach that considers all aspects of something as a whole.
quests.explanation: 'Holistic approach,' 'holistic view,' and 'treat holistically' are key. Used in medicine ('holistic health') and education. The opposite is 'reductionist' - focusing on individual parts.
quests.textToSpeak: The doctors took a ___ approach to her treatment, addressing both body and mind.
quests.correctAnswer: The doctors took a holistic approach to her treatment, addressing both body and mind.

quests.hint: This noun refers to whether something is possible and practical to do successfully.
quests.explanation: 'Study the feasibility,' 'feasibility report,' and 'commercial feasibility' are key. 'Feasible' is the adjective: 'Is this feasible?' 'Feasibility study' assesses whether a project can work.
quests.textToSpeak: A full ___ study was conducted before the board committed funding to the project.
quests.correctAnswer: A full feasibility study was conducted before the board committed funding to the project.

quests.hint: This noun refers to any person or group with an interest in the outcome of a project.
quests.explanation: 'Key stakeholders,' 'engage stakeholders,' and 'stakeholder consultation' are key business terms. 'Shareholder' owns shares; 'stakeholder' is broader - anyone affected by a decision.
quests.textToSpeak: All key ___ were consulted before the final plan was presented to the board.
quests.correctAnswer: All key stakeholders were consulted before the final plan was presented to the board.

quests.hint: This verb means to reduce the severity or seriousness of a problem or risk.
quests.explanation: 'Mitigate risk,' 'mitigate the impact,' and 'mitigation strategy' are key. 'Mitigation' is the noun. Used heavily in climate, law, business, and project management contexts.
quests.textToSpeak: Better planning at the start would have helped to ___ the risks significantly.
quests.correctAnswer: Better planning at the start would have helped to mitigate the risks significantly.

quests.hint: This noun refers to something that causes a rapid or important change or reaction.
quests.explanation: 'Act as a catalyst,' 'catalyst for change,' and 'economic catalyst' are key. Originally a chemistry term - a substance that speeds up a reaction. Now widely used figuratively.
quests.textToSpeak: The crisis acted as a ___ for sweeping and long-overdue reforms across the system.
quests.correctAnswer: The crisis acted as a catalyst for sweeping and long-overdue reforms across the system.

quests.hint: This adjective describes something that is no longer in use because it has been replaced.
quests.explanation: 'Become obsolete,' 'render obsolete,' and 'technologically obsolete' are key. 'Obsolescence' is the noun. 'Planned obsolescence' means products are designed to become outdated.
quests.textToSpeak: Many traditional manufacturing skills have become ___ in the age of automation.
quests.correctAnswer: Many traditional manufacturing skills have become obsolete in the age of automation.

quests.hint: This adjective describes something that no longer serves a purpose or is needed.
quests.explanation: 'Made redundant,' 'redundant staff,' and 'redundancy payment' are key in British employment law. 'Redundant' can also mean unnecessarily repetitive: 'a redundant phrase.'
quests.textToSpeak: After the merger, many positions became ___ and the workforce had to be reduced.
quests.correctAnswer: After the merger, many positions became redundant and the workforce had to be reduced.

quests.hint: This adjective describes someone who has mixed feelings or is uncertain about a choice.
quests.explanation: 'Feel ambivalent,' 'ambivalent about,' and 'a sense of ambivalence' are key. 'Ambivalence' is the noun. 'Ambivalent' differs from 'indifferent' - you care but feel conflicted.
quests.textToSpeak: She felt deeply ___ about leaving the company she had worked at for twelve years.
quests.correctAnswer: She felt deeply ambivalent about leaving the company she had worked at for twelve years.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a natural tendency or inclination to behave in a certain way.
quests.explanation: 'A disposition toward,' 'natural disposition,' and 'sunny disposition' are key. 'Disposition' in law means how something is dealt with. 'Disposed to' means inclined or likely to.
quests.textToSpeak: She has a natural ___ toward optimism that makes her an inspiring person to be around.
quests.correctAnswer: She has a natural disposition toward optimism that makes her an inspiring person to be around.
